description: The New Zealand benefit unit (engine Family entity): an adult, their co-resident partner, and their dependent children; every other adult forms their own unit. An adult for unit construction is any person excluded from the declared dependent-child rule, including a financially independent young person, an independent teen parent, or a household reference person below the age limit with no co-resident parent (child_without_coresident_parent, as amended on 2026-11-15). The unit id family.family_id and membership person.person_family_id are structural graph columns (microcosm.graph.executor._structural_columns); a non-structural node cannot own either (microcosm.graph.executor._validate_population_declaration). family.family_household_id is the ordinary family column linking each unit to its household. The shared transport CREATE kernel (G4/G5a; microcosm.build.transport.population_kernels.TransportCreateKernel) builds units from donor concept pointers under this spec. Family weights are inherited from the household through the Frame.
status: settled by the NZ hub on 2026-10-12 under G8 method addendum B8 (MC7); B8 amended by the NZ hub on 2026-11-15 (child_without_coresident_parent.amendments)

source_household_lineage.rule: Each unit inherits its household's exact original-source key. The donor reader scopes raw source_household_id by source_year, merging support clones across channels; no row-order or support-row-id fallback is permitted.

composition.rule: each person who is not a dependent child anchors exactly one unit unless they join a partner's unit
a co-resident partner (partner_person_id, a symmetric pointer) joins the adult's unit; partners always share a unit

A dependent child joins the unit of its co-resident parent parent_1_person_id; if that parent is itself dependent, follow the parent chain to that parent's unit. A lone co-resident parent is always parent 1 (concepts.py _pointer("parent_1_person_id")), so parent_2_person_id never chooses the unit.
every other adult in the household, including boarders and flatmates, forms their own unit

dependent_child.basis: Social Security Act 2018, Schedule 2, as at 1 April 2026: child (LMS6902), dependent child (LMS7234), single (DLM6784713), and in a relationship (DLM6784537). The statutory definition requires a single person below the age limit and excludes financially independent persons in the declared young-person age range. A household reference person below the age limit with no co-resident parent is also excluded (child_without_coresident_parent); that exclusion is a modelling approximation, not a statutory one (unobserved_statutory_limbs).

financial_independence.basis: Social Security Act 2018, Schedule 2, financially independent (DLM6784504, limb a) and full employment (DLM6784514, limbs a and b), as at 1 April 2026; G8 method addendum B8. The test applies only while below age_limit_years.
financial_independence.concept_evidence: concepts.py concept("fact:person.usual_weekly_hours") declares usual weekly hours across all jobs and self-employment in worked weeks in the donor reference year, with transport CARRY. microcosm.frame.adapters.policyengine_us_concepts.POLICYENGINE_US_CONCEPT_MAPPING maps weekly_hours_worked_before_lsr through Identity to this concept; microcosm.frame.transport.read_populace_us_donor decodes the donor through that mapping. docs/concept-coverage/policyengine-us.md#inputs-each-concept-feeds records the same binding.
financial_independence.approximation: The donor usual rate in worked weeks is used for the statutory average weekly employment test; employment contracts and the averaging interval are not observed.

dependent_child.rulespec_encoding: The executable thresholds and placement decisions are declared in this country spec and read by the shared CREATE kernel. A future RuleSpec encoding of the Schedule 2 definitions can replace this block after its equivalence is reviewed.

child_without_coresident_parent.status: settled by the NZ hub on 2026-10-12, G8 method addendum B8; amended by the NZ hub on 2026-11-15 (amendments)
child_without_coresident_parent.rule: A dependent child with no co-resident parent joins the unit that holds the household reference person. A household reference person below age_limit_years with no co-resident parent is not a dependent child, even when no other declared test makes them independent: they head their own unit, and the dependent children who name them as parent 1, and every dependent child in the household with no co-resident parent, join it. When the reference person is a dependent child with a co-resident parent, a dependent child with no co-resident parent follows the reference person's caregiver chain into the unit that holds the reference person: their parent's unit, or the unit further up the parent chain when that parent is also dependent. No placement is refused because the reference person is below the age limit; the caregiver refusal in refusals still applies.

amendments.change: refuse_dependent_reference_person changed from true to false. With true, the shared constructor refused the whole frame in two cases: (i) the reference person is below the age limit, has no co-resident parent and is not otherwise independent, so the constructor kept them dependent and treated them as their own child with no co-resident parent; (ii) the reference person is a dependent child with a co-resident parent, and the household holds another dependent child with no co-resident parent. Case (ii) is the refusal B8 states; case (i) was the constructor's reading of it. This amendment drops both refusals.
amendments.reason: The strict reading refused real donor households. The check runs over the whole frame, so one such household aborted the frame build, and the first real-data NZ transport run stopped on it. Literal B8 would still refuse case (ii), and the declaration has no setting that keeps case (ii) while dropping case (i); that would need a change to the shared constructor.
amendments.measured: Measured on the pinned donor with the CREATE kernel's own reader and this declaration: 9 of 57,240 households, 0.0024% of household weight, tripped the refusal. 6 are case (ii): a reference person aged 15 or 16 with a parent present, and another child with no co-resident parent. 3 are case (i): a reference person aged 16 or 17 with no co-resident parent. Each of the 9 has a member aged 18 or over; none is a household of minors only. Without these 9 households the strict rule builds the frame. With this amendment the whole frame builds: each case (i) reference person heads a one-person unit, and in each case (ii) household the child with no co-resident parent joins the unit of the reference person's parent, which no minor heads. Of the frame's 378 unit heads aged 17 or under, these 3 are the only ones heading a unit through this branch; the others are adults under the partner, teen-parent or hours tests.
amendments.accommodation_supplement: A minor who heads a unit through this branch reads as a sole parent when the unit also holds a dependent child: their own child when they are below parent_independence_min_age, or another child with no co-resident parent. family.is_sole_parent and family.n_dependent_children, the Accommodation Supplement inputs accommodation_supplement_sole_parent, accommodation_supplement_has_dependent_children and accommodation_supplement_has_two_or_more_dependent_children (unit_composition transforms in concept_mapping.json), and the rate bridge (as_rate_bridge.json) read that composition. The person-level inputs read parent pointers, so they count no sibling as that person's child. On the pinned donor the 3 new heads are one-person units, so no Accommodation Supplement input reads a minor as a sole parent through this branch. In case (ii) the unit of the reference person's parent holds one more dependent child.
amendments.receipt: The CREATE receipt (microcosm.frame.unit_construction.benefit_unit_diagnostics) counts the persons below age_limit_years who head a unit through this branch as parentless_reference_person_heads, and counts a parent below parent_independence_min_age who heads a unit this way, or who has a co-resident partner, as younger_independent_teen_parents, so the three teen-parent counts partition the parents below age_limit_years (unit_construction_diagnostics).

refusals: a unit whose members span two households
a parent or partner pointer to a person outside the household
a dependent child in a household with no adult

a dependent child whose caregivers never reach an adult (parent 1, or the household reference person for a child with no co-resident parent, followed through dependent caregivers), as when a reference person who is a dependent child has a parent 1 below parent_independence_min_age with no co-resident parent or partner
invariants: every person is in exactly one unit
every unit has at least one adult
every dependent child shares a unit with a parent or the reference person
sum of family weights equals the sum over households of household weight times units in the household

unit_attributes.note: Unit attributes the planned unit-attributes node (transport.unit_attributes@1, package G5a) is to emit on the family entity, for the reg 17/18 bridge and the group encode to read. The bridge's adults_in_couple multiplier (as_rate_bridge.json) is not declared here yet; the bridge kernels (package G7) are to settle it.

columns.family.family_type: category of the MC7 unit: single, couple, sole parent, couple with children
columns.family.n_dependent_children: count of dependent children in the unit
columns.family.is_sole_parent: single adult with at least one dependent child
columns.family.is_partnered: the unit contains a partnered couple
columns.family.is_single: the unit has one adult (not family.is_partnered)
columns.family.youngest_dependent_child_age: age of the youngest dependent child; null when there is none

settlement_basis: docs/nz-benefit-unit-rule.md (the NZ hub's G8 method note B8, settled 2026-10-12 and amended 2026-11-15)

teen_parent.at_or_above_parent_independence_min_age: A person below age_limit_years with a co-resident child of their own forms their own unit with that child once at or above parent_independence_min_age.
teen_parent.below_parent_independence_min_age: The parent rule does not make a younger parent independent; the other declared tests decide. With a co-resident parent they remain dependent in their own parent's unit, and their child joins that same unit. Without one, the declared reference-person placement applies: they join the unit that holds the household reference person, or, when they are the reference person, they head their own unit and a child who names them as parent 1 joins it (child_without_coresident_parent, as amended on 2026-11-15).
teen_parent.basis: Settled by the NZ hub on 2026-10-12, G8 method addendum B8. Young Parent Payment is a main benefit; Schedule 2 financially independent (DLM6784504, limb d) excludes its recipient from child. Unit construction infers the older teen-parent exclusion from the co-resident parent pointer before the receipt layer runs; receipt is not observed or assigned by this rule.
teen_parent.placement_of_the_child: These branches decide whether the teen parent is a dependent child. When the child's two co-resident parents end up in separate units, the child follows the declared parent-1 placement (split_parents).

non_partnered_coparents.rule: The dependent child joins parent 1's unit when its two co-resident parents are not partners.
non_partnered_coparents.basis: Settled by the NZ hub on 2026-10-12, G8 method addendum B8; preserves the declared first-parent placement.

unobserved_statutory_limbs.omission: Student-allowance basic grants and independent-circumstances grants are not observable in the transported donor; this exclusion is not applied.
Payments from analogous Government-assisted schemes are not observable in the transported donor; this exclusion is not applied.

Main-benefit receipt is assigned after unit construction and does not otherwise exclude a young person. The declared teen-parent branch is the disclosed exception, inferred from co-resident child pointers before receipt assignment.
An award, agreement, or contract deeming employment full time at fewer hours is not observable; this exclusion is not applied.
Orphan's benefit and unsupported child's benefit receipt are not identifiable in the donor. These children remain dependent in the unit they join; the statutory exclusion is not applied.

unobserved_statutory_limbs.definition: dependent child (LMS7234, limbs a(i), a(ii), and a(iii))
unobserved_statutory_limbs.omission: Primary responsibility, maintenance and financial dependency are represented by household and parent placement rather than observed care or support. Oranga Tamariki payments and placements, and a young parent payment to a caregiver who is not the child's parent or step-parent, are not identifiable; their statutory distinctions are not applied.

unobserved_statutory_limbs.definition: single (DLM6784713) and in a relationship (DLM6784537), as used in child (LMS6902); section 8 (DLM6783126)
unobserved_statutory_limbs.omission: Statutory single status is approximated by the co-resident partner pointer (partner_person_id). A married, civil-union or de facto young person whose spouse or partner does not live in the household is treated as single and can be placed as a dependent child. Legal marital status is not recovered by the donor decoder, and MSD determinations under section 8 that a person is or is not single are not observable; neither is applied.

unobserved_statutory_limbs.definition: child (LMS6902) and dependent child (LMS7234), for a household reference person below the age limit with no co-resident parent
unobserved_statutory_limbs.omission: Unit construction does not treat this person as a dependent child: they head their own unit, and the dependent children who name them as parent 1, and any dependent child in the household with no co-resident parent, join it (child_without_coresident_parent, amended by the NZ hub on 2026-11-15). This is a modelling approximation, not a statutory exclusion. The Act makes no exception for a household reference person; the pointers name no co-resident person whose dependent child they could be, and who has primary responsibility for them is not observed. It applies at any age below age_limit_years, so it can make a person under 16 the head of a unit.

unit_construction_diagnostics.hours_independent_children: Count of otherwise dependent candidates at or above financial_independence.min_age and below age_limit_years excluded by min_usual_weekly_hours.
unit_construction_diagnostics.independent_teen_parents: Count of persons below age_limit_years with a co-resident child, at or above parent_independence_min_age, excluded from dependency by the parent rule.
unit_construction_diagnostics.younger_independent_teen_parents: Count of persons with a co-resident child, below parent_independence_min_age, who are not dependent children because another branch applies: a co-resident partner, or heading their own unit as a parentless household reference person. With independent_teen_parents and dependent_teen_parents it partitions the persons below age_limit_years who have a co-resident child.
unit_construction_diagnostics.dependent_teen_parents: Count of persons with a co-resident child below parent_independence_min_age who remain dependent under the declared rules.
unit_construction_diagnostics.non_partnered_coparent_households: Count of distinct households containing a dependent child with two co-resident parents who are not partners; count a household once even when several children qualify.
unit_construction_diagnostics.children_with_reference_person: Count of dependent children with no co-resident parent placed in the unit that holds the household reference person.
unit_construction_diagnostics.parentless_reference_person_heads: Count of household reference persons below age_limit_years with no co-resident parent whom neither a partner nor the hours or parent rules exclude from dependency; each heads their own unit because refuse_dependent_reference_person is false.
